Budget.description: An envelope money is divided into. Amounts are decimal strings.

balance.description: What the allocations add up to, or the bank account's balance when assigned.

Budget.title: Budget

BudgetRequest.description:
Amounts are decimal strings. `balance` is what the user wants the budget to hold - the server
works out the adjustment that gets it there, so never send `adjustment`.
BudgetRequest.title: BudgetRequest

BudgetSummary.description:
Everything the budgets screen shows for one month. Presentation is the client's - this is the
numbers behind it.

current_month.description: Spendable, allocated and credit cards only apply to the current month.

spendable.description: Synced money no budget has claimed.

spent.description: Spent this month, keyed by budget id. Every listed budget has an entry.

spent_by_month.description: Newest first, for the month picker.

BudgetSummary.title: BudgetSummary

BulkRequest.description:
Applies the same change to several transactions. `budget_id` spends each transaction's whole
amount from that budget, replacing whatever it was allocated to before.
BulkRequest.title: BulkRequest

BulkResult.description:
A bulk change is applied per transaction rather than all or nothing, so the ones that worked
come back alongside the ones that did not.
BulkResult.title: BulkResult

Errors.description: The shape every failed request comes back in.

source.description: Present on validation errors, pointing at the offending field.

Errors.title: Errors

Session.description: An API token. The token itself is returned once and never again.
Session.title: Session

SessionRequest.description: An ID token from a native sign-in, exchanged for an API token.
SessionRequest.title: SessionRequest

Split.description: A saved division of a transaction across budgets. Amounts are decimal strings.
Split.title: Split

SplitRequest.description:
Send the whole set of lines you want the split to end up with. A line with an `id` is kept and
updated, one without is added, and any line left out is deleted.

id.description: Omit to add a new line.

SplitRequest.title: SplitRequest

Transaction.description:
A movement of money. Amounts are decimal strings, negative for money going out.

`budget_allocations` is what the server settled on, not what was sent: any part of the amount
left unallocated lands on the Spendable budget on every write. Render what comes back.

transfer_id.description: The other side of a move between the user's own accounts.

Transaction.title: Transaction

TransactionRequest.description:
Send the whole set of allocations you want. One with an `id` is kept and updated, one without
is added, one left out is deleted. Whatever is left of the amount goes to Spendable, so the
allocations in the response are the ones that count.

That also means a validation error's pointer indexes the list the server settled on, not the
one that was sent - match the offending line by its `budget_id`, not by position.

id.description: Omit to add a new allocation.

TransactionRequest.title: TransactionRequest

TransactionSource.description:
Where a synced transaction came from, flattened for the list row. Null on a transaction the
user entered themselves. Fetch the logo from `/api/banks/{member_id}/logo`.
TransactionSource.title: TransactionSource

TransferRequest.description: Exactly two transactions: one leaving an account and one arriving in another.
TransferRequest.title: TransferRequest

bank_limit.description: How many banks the user may connect.

info.description: The API the Spendable mobile app runs on.
info.title: Spendable

get.description: Spendable first, then alphabetical. Archived budgets are left out.
Defaults to the current month. Any date in a month selects that whole month.
get.summary: The budgets screen for one month

delete.description: Budgets are archived rather than deleted, so the history they hold survives.

patch.description: The response carries the recalculated balance, so render it rather than the request.

put.description: The response carries the recalculated balance, so render it rather than the request.

delete.description: Revokes the token the request was made with.

post.description: Exchanges an ID token from a native sign-in for an API token.

get.description: Alphabetical, without their lines. Archived splits are left out.

get.summary: Get a split and its lines

get.description:
Newest first. Reviewed and excluded transactions are hidden unless asked for, because the list
is a queue of what still needs attention. A page shorter than `per_page` is the last one.

post.description: For money the user is recording themselves; synced activity arrives on its own.

patch.description:
Applied one at a time rather than all or nothing, so a transaction that has since been deleted
does not cost the rest their change. Check `failed` before assuming the whole set landed.

post.description:
A transfer moves money between the user's own accounts rather than spending it, so the pair
has to be one transaction leaving an account and one arriving in another. Both sides come
back, with their allocations cleared onto Spendable where the opposite signs cancel.
post.summary: Link two transactions as a transfer

patch.description: The response carries the allocations the server settled on. Render those.

put.description: The response carries the allocations the server settled on. Render those.

delete.description: Both sides count toward budgets again. Their allocations stay where they are.
